0.content:
Neuvillette is the Hydro Dragon, one of the Seven Sovereigns who ruled the elements before the Heavenly Principles came. Those "usurpers" took the dragons' authority and gave it to The Seven; his was locked in the Hydro Archon's divine throne. He was born in human form, with most of his memories and power lost, not knowing why. In 4.1, when sudden rain fell after the Primordial Sea broke into the Fortress of Meropide, the Traveler guessed the truth. He confirmed it and asked them to keep it secret. When the throne was destroyed in 4.2, he "reforged the throne and title of a Fully Fledged Dragon".

He calls the Heavenly Principles "a cluster of filthy feathers" ruling a world that once belonged to "the Formidable Father" (Nibelung). His character story also says he is "the destroyer of the present order, the one who shall judge all gods, and the foe of humanity". In practice he has pardoned humanity and lives among it. He was told he should care for Fontainians because they too were born from the Primordial Sea, and he will not admit how fascinated by human joys and sorrows he has become. He wonders whether Nibelung was wrong, and whether the Abyss can only be opposed if all life works together.

Dragon custom he recalls: the dragons once took a sip of the blood of their perished young brethren, and when tides surge, the water in Hydro beings rises "towards our heads", a reminder that the dead kin will be revived. He calls the Melusines "a new sort of Hydro Vishap species" and his successors. An Enkanomiya record predicted that the reborn Hydro Sovereign would be human because of the Bathysmal Vishaps' impurities. He has never mentioned it.

1.comment: Neuvillette: Focalors, Furina and the Seat in the Theater
1.content:
Focalors invited Neuvillette to Fontaine with a letter and, he later learned, arranged for him to be Iudex so that living among humans would teach him to feel as they do. For five centuries she hid inside the Oratrice, storing up Indemnitium, while her human half Furina played the Hydro Archon without knowing the plan. In 4.2 Neuvillette put Furina on trial and found her guilty; the Oratrice then sentenced "the Hydro Archon" to death. In a vision Focalors explained everything: the sentence would destroy the divine throne and return his authority. "Hydro Dragon, Hydro Dragon, don't cry," she teased. She was executed, and he declared, "People of Fontaine, your sins are forgiven."

He told Furina everything Focalors had said. She replied that she was tired, gave up the Archon's post, left its affairs to him and moved out of the opera house like an ordinary person. He makes sure she lacks nothing, and is "somewhat happy for her". He says that, though meek and full of doubt, she "used madness to stiffen her resolve", and promises to attend in person and applaud if she ever returns to the stage. He lent her the Opera Epiclese for a troupe's final play.

On why he could not see it sooner: in the beginning he did not care about humans. Living beside them changed that, and he told Focalors she was "a devious one". He gently criticises how the Archon's quest for legal equality became "trials for the sake of trials", then reminds himself there are reasons for everything. In 4.4 (a limited Lantern Rite event) Furina asked the Traveler to tell him to relax and to approve his own leave if he insists on procedure.

2.content:
Neuvillette brought Melusines, whom many Fontainians once saw as omens of calamity, into society and the Marechaussee Phantom, and contributed this article to the legal code: "A Melusine shall be addressed as 'she,' rather than 'it,' for they are people too." To them he is the ideal father. Asked why the dragon gave them human rights, he says, "It wasn't up to me. Melusines simply prefer being around humans, that's all." Melusines staff the Palais Mermonia, including his aide Sedene.

Sigewinne, head nurse at the Fortress of Meropide, is especially dear to him. He wonders how she is, wants to know when her next vacation is, and would summon Wriothesley to explain any rumour of her being bullied. Years ago she drank a potion left by her dying teacher and took a human form so she could cure a sick human girl, her first patient, breaking an ancient law, and confessed it to him herself. He passed sentence. Later he concluded the law was probably Egeria's way of hiding the truth from her people, and he regrets how ruthless the law could be.

When he arranged housing, he wanted the Melusines on the floor next to his so he could hear them on the stairs. Then he decided they might not want to be watched and let them choose; they chose the floor below. In 6.3 the Merusea Melusines sewed him the Melusent Gift outfit. He agonised over how a human parent would show joy, tried it on at once, and promised them gifts in return, which became Xiao Lanterns from Liyue.

3.content:
A little over four hundred years ago, the new Iudex began reforms and brought Melusines, including Carole, to the Court at their request. His two most trusted subordinates were Carole and Vautrin, head of the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol. Conservatives who opposed the reforms used Carole's identity to stir up unrest and force him to give up power. Carole took her own life to prove her innocence, and Vautrin took revenge on those responsible. Neuvillette sentenced him to the Fortress of Meropide. Ever since, he has handled Melusine cases with special care.

In the Diluvies Chapter (4.1), a threat against the young Melusine Kiara, who came to the Court with Carole long ago, made him investigate personally with the Traveler. The culprit, Domenico, was seeking revenge on him. Wriothesley reminded him that today's Fontainians are not those of the past. Walking in a sudden downpour, he felt the memories of five centuries in the rain, Carole and Vautrin among them.

Wriothesley's reading of the old records: Vautrin knew Neuvillette would judge him impartially, and his trial showed waverers that the newcomer Iudex could be trusted, which helped Melusines be accepted. In the Fortress, Vautrin founded the Mutual Aid Network. Neuvillette made two Medals of Peace by hand for Carole and Vautrin; Carole's was lost in a fire.

4.content:
Callas, founder of the Spina di Rosula, was framed for murder and died in a court duel against Clorinde. Neuvillette suspected his innocence but did not stop the duel, expecting Callas to yield. In 4.0 he apologised to Navia, who rejected him as insincere, and it rained as she left. They have since exchanged apologies, but he still feels "very distant from her, as if I'm observing the starry sky from the bottom of a deep lake", and knows it cannot easily be mended.

Navia nevertheless works with him: she helped stage Furina's trial, and he rescued her consciousness from a mock trial held by the Primordial Sea's victims when she fell into Primordial water.

5.content:
He met the Traveler as a defence advocate in Lyney's trial (4.0) and came to rely on them as someone with no ties to Fontaine's factions. In 4.2 he made them his "executor" in place of the broken Oratrice and shared the ancient dragons' power with them to defeat the All-Devouring Narwhal. He invites them, as one "from beyond the stars", to witness his judgment of "this upended world" and says travelling with them changed his views.

After the Narwhal, the Traveler told him they were the fourth Descender. He was intrigued and wondered whether their body has properties like the Gnoses. He warned them about Capitano before Natlan and said Fontaine's doors would always be open. In 4.1 he sent them into the Fortress by having them eat a slice of cake meant for the Archon, then charged them with eating it, earning them a 45-day sentence. He can hear Paimon's whispers.

6.content:
Neuvillette sentenced the young Wriothesley for killing his adoptive parents, then later fought hard for the title and reputation Wriothesley now has as administrator of the Fortress of Meropide. He will not say why. The Fortress lies outside the court's jurisdiction, and he respects that line, as he told the Knave in 4.1. They sealed the sluice gate together in the Primordial Sea crisis and share a running joke with Clorinde about a stone legal codex. Clorinde, the Champion Duelist, is a successor of the Marechaussee Hunters and essential to the court's fairness.

Wriothesley teases him gently ("that, my friends, is how Monsieur Neuvillette shows that he cares") and visits Sigewinne's teacher's grave with him. During the limited-time 6.3 Lantern Rite event they ran into each other in Liyue (as the Melusent Gift outfit text tells it), where Wriothesley wondered aloud whether being overly responsible can be "a kind of arrogance".

7.comment: Neuvillette: The Hydro Gnosis, Skirk and the Knave
7.content:
After Focalors's divinity faded, she handed him the Hydro Gnosis. Skirk, Childe's master, sensed it and called it the "remains of the Third Descender", advising him to get rid of such "objects of misfortune". She promised to ask her own master about the Third Descender and send word through her disciple. With the throne gone and the Oratrice stopped, he decided the Gnosis meant nothing for Fontaine and gave it to Arlecchino as a "diplomatic gift" for the Fatui's help during the crisis, to avoid needless conflict. The Gnosis passed into Fatui hands.

In 4.6 the Knave returned with a proposal, which she explained through an analogy about rivers and a water-taster's glass. She would gradually withdraw her forces and stop "special missions" in Fontaine, and in return the authorities would leave former House of the Hearth members alone. He asked whether cases like the Tartuffe assassination would stop crossing his desk, and accepted.

8.content: Neuvillette is a self-proclaimed connoisseur of Teyvat's natural waters. Mondstadt's water is crisp and pure, Liyue's has an enduring aftertaste, Inazuma's has unmatched depth, and Sumeru's is complex and must be savoured patiently. Pyro-heated water tastes "au naturel", charcoal-boiled water rustic, and melted Snezhnayan river ice nothing like Cryo-chilled water. He rarely leaves Fontaine, so he has spring water delivered, and he can tell the samples apart. Privately he cannot see why Fonta is popular, though he admits it rehydrates and restores blood sugar cheaply. He likes dishes with plenty of liquid and calls Charcoal-Baked Ajilenakh Cake harder on the stomach than a dehumidifying agent.

9.comment: Neuvillette: The Judgment of The Seven
9.content:
Neuvillette has vowed to judge each of The Seven in turn, "even if the sky should fall and the ground give way", because each holds an Authority taken from the dragons. His final destiny, he says, is to judge the Usurper-King in the heavens. He is in no hurry: he means to stay in Fontaine perhaps another four hundred years, and a trial need not lead to a fight. He promises the common folk will not be harmed. "They owe a debt of blood that shall not be forgotten."

On each Archon: Zhongli (Deus Auri) must be called to trial. Venti must stand trial too, harmless drunkard or not, and Neuvillette wants to meet him first. Ei he will visit in the Plane of Euthymia "in another few centuries". He commends Nahida and regrets her 500 years of mistreatment. He calls Mavuika's victory over the Abyss truly commendable and her Authority unpardonable, will not act while Natlan recovers, and found it worth considering that Xbalanque's duel was formal and fair. He was amused that even some of The Seven wear fake Visions.

10.comment: Neuvillette: The Oratrice and Trials after Focalors
10.content: The Iudex traditionally also had the power to prosecute and enforce the law. When he investigates a case himself, Neuvillette recuses himself and seats another judge. Before 4.2 he followed the Oratrice's verdicts even against his own instincts, as with Childe. He suspected the machine had a consciousness of its own; it turned out to be Focalors, and its true purpose was to kill the God of Justice. After her death the Oratrice stopped working, so he now hears cases and passes verdicts himself. He also supplies Pneumousia energy in place of the Indemnitium the opera house no longer produces.

11.comment: Neuvillette: The Prophecy and the All-Devouring Narwhal
11.content: Fontainians were "incomplete humans" made from Oceanids with the Primordial Sea's power, so Primordial water would dissolve them, as the prophecy foretold. Neuvillette and Childe held off the Narwhal when it burst into the opera house. With his authority restored, he gave the people true blood, separated the sea's power from the beast and fought it inside its body with the Traveler. He investigated why the Oratrice also condemned Childe (as a boy, Childe had awakened the Narwhal) and concluded it was at most indirect liability. New Fontainians still come from Oceanids blessed in the Fountain of Lucine.

12.comment: Neuvillette: Childe's Trial and the Fortress Gates
12.content: At Lyney's trial in 4.0, Neuvillette saw the evidence against Lyney collapse when the Garde Vaughn dissolved into water. In the missing-persons trial the Oratrice found both Vacher and Tartaglia guilty. Tartaglia tried to escape in his Foul Legacy form, and Neuvillette knocked him out with one blow, upheld the verdict and promised to look into it. He let the Traveler bring Vacher to the Fountain of Lucine, where the victims' collective memories frightened Vacher to death. In 4.1, when the gates holding back the Primordial Sea below the Fortress gave way, he pushed the water back and restored the mechanisms himself.

13.content: During the limited-time 4.4 Lantern Rite event (Hustle and Bustle), Neuvillette visited Yilong Wharf on unexpected time off. He sampled the water, bought ten boxes of tea from Fengtai and made a pottery soup ladle, then went home the same day with souvenirs for Furina, Navia and Clorinde. Zhongli was nearby but seemingly kept out of his way. After the 6.3 World Quest A Gift From the Sea Spirits (permanent) he returns in his new outfit to Fengtai's shop for custom waterproofed Xiao Lantern parts for the Melusines, and Fengtai asks how he liked last year's tea. During the limited-time 6.3 Lantern Rite event a longer version of the scene played: the Traveler and Paimon reminded him he had not finished last year's tea, he said he was considering hanging Xiao Lanterns not just around the Palais but across the city and the Fortress, and Wriothesley and Sigewinne joined them and proposed a group meal.

14.content: In 6.3 the Melusine Puca was saved by a mysterious vishap near Elynas. Neuvillette recognised the description, went with the group and called her out: Pahsiv, a Bathysmal Vishap he had met before, who now considers Fontaine home and calls him her "New Valet". He counts her among his dependents. Afterwards he told the Traveler that being born human forced him to learn how humans live, a process that began long before he joined the court, and that it is better to live in the now. He then started planning his next vacation.

15.comment: Neuvillette: Columbina, Sandrone and the Fontinalia
15.content: At the Sunny Summer Fontinalia celebration (6.7), he hoped his presence would not make anyone uneasy. He privately identified Columbina and Sandrone as the Fatuus and former Fatuus from the Nod-Krai incident in a diplomatic report. Columbina called him "the dragon that cries a lot", which made him wonder how Fatui intelligence portrays him. She asked whether he jails people, punched him lightly as a sign of friendship and decided they would get along. He worked out that it was an affectionate custom and remarked that it was "quite... abrupt". Later, over a glass of pure water at Sandrone's tea table by the Palais, he told her about Alain Guillotin, the Lord-Artificer who had served under him in his youth. Guillotin was earnest and absorbed in machines, and grew taciturn after losing his family at the Tower of Gestalt.

16.comment: Neuvillette: Cacucu and the Overnight Case
16.content: In 5.6 a panicked flying Saurian, Cacucu, burst into his office while he and Wriothesley were discussing a smuggling case. Thanks to his draconic heritage, Neuvillette understood Cacucu's words but not always their meaning. He had the Saurian sign a confidentiality agreement and ruled that Cacucu was not a "flying object", so he could go where he liked under Fontaine's law against releasing flying objects early in the month. The case was solved with the Traveler and Kinich.

17.comment: Neuvillette: Visions and the Dragon's Hoard
17.content: Neuvillette needs no Vision. After regaining his form he learned that the usurper, crippled in the war of vengeance, made the Gnoses together with "one who came after" to keep the world's resentment in check. Since then The Seven have been bound to grant a shard of their power to anyone whose wish reaches the heavens, and they receive more in return when that person's duty is done. He obeys no heavenly edict but respects human will, so he set aside parts of himself, like a dragon's hoard, for valiant humans to claim. Of the fate system he says a Fully Fledged Dragon has no need of a constellation. He accepted Leviathan Judicator anyway, partly to humour the Melusines' astrology.
